messages.subject: Possible bug(s) in Stan?
parts:
So this may be triggering one or more bugs in Stan. I'll try to explain why. I've gotten down to the C++ level and started digging.

  • (good) I was able to compile the model without a problem.
  • (good) I can run diagnose mode with init=0 without a problem.
  • (good) Diagnose works most times and finishes in a reasonable amount of time.
  • (BAD) Diagnose doesn't work sometimes. It ends up in what seems to be an infinite loop. It's stuck in the log_prob_grad function in src/stan/model/util.hpp.
    • possible bug 1: val ends up as nan in this code
              var adLogProb
                = model
                .template log_prob<propto,
                                   jacobian_adjust_transform>(ad_params_r,
                                                              params_i,msgs);
              double val = adLogProb.val();
    • should this really be allowed to be nan without throwing an exception? If so, we need to stop the execution here.
    • possible bug 2: I think it gets into an infinite loop here
              adLogProb.grad(ad_params_r,gradient);
    • It gets into the grad function, but never exits. I'm guessing there's a bug in here somewhere.
  • (BAD) Every so often diagnose doesn't work, but exits with
    Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts.
     Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.


I haven't really gone through this model in too much depth, but for the purposes of finding which bugs this touches on, I don't think we need the full model.

What I'm going to try to do is create a unit test that demonstrates the possible infinite loop. If anyone wants to help, I would appreciate it.


Daniel

RhoImp~lkj_corr(2);

        }

The infinite loop is in:

gamma_q_vv_vari::chain()

Instruments picked it up in no time.

The offending loop appears to be this one:

while (std::fabs(delta) > 1e-6) {
...
}

We can't just assume iterative algorithms will terminate.
They need to count iterations of the loop and terminate after
some finite number of steps and throw a non-convergence error.

I'll track it down a bit more closely and create the issue and a branch
with a unit test that fails. But I'm not even sure what this function
is, so I don't think I should be the one to fix it!

- Bob
